propositions.text: The appellant appeals a Federal Court order dismissing her motion to continue a class action via fresh certification motion.
propositions.quote: The appellant, Ms. Berenguer, appeals an order and reasons of the Federal Court dated June 3, 2025... dismissing her motion to determine what rights she had, if any, to continue her proposed class action via a fresh motion for certification.

propositions.text: Federal Court applied functus officio and res judicata (issue estoppel) doctrines and found no remedial jurisdiction to reopen certification motion.
propositions.quote: Applying the doctrines of functus officio and res judicata in the form of issue estoppel, the Federal Court found that it had no remedial jurisdiction to re-open the certification motion and refused to exercise its discretion to set aside issue estoppel.

propositions.text: Federal Court concluded appellant could not bring a second certification motion relying on Rules 385(1) and 334.2 of Federal Courts Rules.
propositions.quote: The Court concluded that Ms. Berenguer could not bring a second certification motion in reliance on Rules 385(1) and 334.2 of the Federal Courts Rules, S.O.R./98-106 (the Rules).

paragraphs.summary: The court states the appellant appeals a Federal Court order dismissing her motion to continue a class action, which applied issue estoppel and refused a second certification motion.

propositions.text: In 2021, Federal Court struck statement of claim for no reasonable cause and dismissed certification motion for failing preferable procedure criterion.
propositions.quote: Very briefly, in 2021, the Federal Court: (a) struck Ms. Berenguer’s statement of claim...; and (b) dismissed Ms. Berenguer’s certification motion for failure to meet the preferable procedure criterion in Rule 334.16(1)(d)

propositions.text: On appeal, this Court set aside striking order but upheld dismissal of certification motion due to insufficient evidence on preferable procedure.
propositions.quote: On appeal, this Court set aside the order striking the statement of claim but found no error... and upheld the dismissal of the certification motion

propositions.text: This Court dismissed appellant's motion to reconsider the FCA Appeal Decision.
propositions.quote: This Court also dismissed Ms. Berenguer’s motion to reconsider the FCA Appeal Decision (FCA Reconsideration Order).

paragraphs.summary: The court recounts the 2021 Federal Court striking and dismissal, the appellate court's partial reversal and upholding of certification dismissal, and dismissal of reconsideration motion.

propositions.text: Appellant seeks to adduce new evidence in this appeal.
propositions.quote: Ms. Berenguer seeks to adduce new evidence in this appeal

propositions.text: The court will dismiss appellant's motion to admit new evidence for failing Palmer criteria and fairness considerations.
propositions.quote: we will dismiss her motion. Although the new evidence was not available... Ms. Berenguer has not satisfied the criteria for admission set out in Palmer v. R.

propositions.text: Admitting new evidence is not fair or just or in interests of justice, as it attempts to remedy original lack of evidence after five years.
propositions.quote: It is clearly not fair or just, or in the interests of justice, to admit the new evidence... The motion is an attempt by Ms. Berenguer to remedy the lack of evidence originally presented and, five years after the Certification Decision, to rely on evidence...

paragraphs.summary: The appellant seeks to introduce new evidence, but the court dismisses the motion for failing admission criteria and fairness, noting delay and remedial intent.

propositions.text: Appellant argues Federal Court erred in law on issue estoppel conditions and discretion to set it aside.
propositions.quote: Ms. Berenguer raises two main issues on appeal. She argues that the Federal Court erred in law (1) in finding the first condition for issue estoppel...; and (2) in failing to exercise its discretion to set aside issue estoppel.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the Federal Court erred in law on issue estoppel conditions and discretion to set it aside.

propositions.text: Standards of review are correctness for pure law and palpable and overriding error for mixed fact and law or fact.
propositions.quote: The applicable standards of review in this appeal are as follows: correctness on pure questions of law... and palpable and overriding error on factually suffused findings of mixed fact and law and findings of fact

paragraphs.summary: The court states the standards of review applicable: correctness for law, palpable and overriding error for mixed fact and law or fact.

propositions.text: The court sees no basis to intervene and will dismiss the appeal.
propositions.quote: For the following reasons, we see no basis to intervene in the FC Order and will dismiss the appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes it will dismiss the appeal and not intervene in the Federal Court order.

propositions.text: Appellant argues Federal Court erred in law finding the same question was addressed at certification, denying first Danyluk condition for issue estoppel.
propositions.quote: Ms. Berenguer first argues that the Federal Court erred in law in concluding that the question she now raises was addressed at certification, such that the first of the three ‘Danyluk’ conditions for the application of issue estoppel was not met

propositions.text: Appellant says remedial question on rectifying evidentiary deficiencies in CTA complaint handling is new and not foreclosed by FCA Reconsideration Order.
propositions.quote: Ms. Berenguer states that the remedial question of whether she should “be permitted to rectify the evidentiary deficiencies in the CTA’s complaint handling capacity” is a new question that was specifically not foreclosed by the FCA Reconsideration Order.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the Federal Court erred in law on issue estoppel's first condition and that a remedial question is new and not foreclosed.

propositions.text: There is no merit to appellant's claim of an unaddressed remedial question; issue estoppel extends to necessarily determined facts and mixed law and fact conclusions.
propositions.quote: There is no merit to Ms. Berenguer’s assertion of an unaddressed remedial question... the estoppel extends to material facts and the conclusions of mixed fact and law… that were necessarily (even if not explicitly) determined in the earlier proceeding

propositions.text: Questions of preferable procedure and required evidence were clearly and necessarily in issue before the Federal Court.
propositions.quote: The questions of preferable procedure and the evidence required to establish it were very clearly and necessarily in issue before the Federal Court.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no merit in appellant's claim of a new remedial question; preferable procedure was necessarily addressed before.

propositions.text: The Federal Court did not err in law by not referring to Supreme Court's Sanis decision; FC Order is not contrary to Sanis.
propositions.quote: we are not persuaded by Ms. Berenguer’s argument that the Federal Court erred in law in failing to refer to the Supreme Court’s decision in Sanis Health Inc. v. British Columbia... The FC Order is not contrary to Sanis.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no error in the Federal Court's failure to refer to Sanis; the order is not contrary to that decision.

propositions.text: Appellant relies on Sanis for certifying court's supervisory jurisdiction and duty to protect class interests after certification dismissal.
propositions.quote: Ms. Berenguer focusses on the Supreme Court’s reference to a certifying court’s general supervisory jurisdiction over a class proceeding and obligation to “make sure the interests of the class members are protected”

propositions.text: The cited Sanis phrase is out of context; Sanis does not establish new framework for certifying court after certification dismissal.
propositions.quote: However, the partial phrase cited is taken out of context. The Supreme Court did not establish a new framework for a certifying court’s role after dismissing a motion for certification

propositions.text: Sanis does not suggest issue estoppel can be overcome by continuing duty to class members in failed class proceeding.
propositions.quote: nor does the Sanis decision suggest that issue estoppel can be overcome by an overarching and continuing duty to class members in a failed class proceeding.

propositions.text: Federal Court was not required to consider adjournment or grant current motion to 'cooper up' certification motion.
propositions.quote: The Federal Court was not required during the certification hearing to consider whether to order an adjournment and permit Ms. Berenguer “to cooper up” her certification motion... nor was it required to grant the current motion.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant's reliance on Sanis misplaced; Sanis does not create new post-certification duties or override issue estoppel.

propositions.text: Appellant's reliance on Rules 385 and 334.2 for continuing jurisdiction is misplaced; no error in Court's analysis of these Rules.
propositions.quote: Ms. Berenguer’s reliance on Rules 385 and 334.2 as a basis for the Federal Court’s continuing jurisdiction is misplaced. We find no error in the Court’s analysis of the two Rules.

propositions.text: Rules 385 and 334.2 do not override issue estoppel doctrine; no conflation of functus officio and issue estoppel by Federal Court.
propositions.quote: Rules 385 and 334.2, correctly interpreted, do not override the doctrine of issue estoppel. We find no conflation of the doctrines of functus officio and issue estoppel by the Federal Court.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no error in the Federal Court's interpretation of Rules 385 and 334.2, which do not override issue estoppel.

propositions.text: No error of law or palpable and overriding error in Federal Court's issue estoppel analysis or conclusion that it applied.
propositions.quote: In summary, we find no error of law or palpable and overriding error in the Federal Court’s analysis of the doctrine of issue estoppel or in its conclusion that issue estoppel had been engaged.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no error in the Federal Court's issue estoppel analysis or conclusion that issue estoppel applied.

propositions.text: Appellant submits Federal Court erred in failing to exercise discretion to set aside issue estoppel and allow reargument of certification motion.
propositions.quote: Ms. Berenguer also submits that the Federal Court erred in failing to exercise its discretion to set aside issue estoppel in this case and to allow her certification motion to be reargued.

propositions.text: The court does not agree with appellant's submission on discretion to set aside issue estoppel.
propositions.quote: Again, we do not agree.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant submits error in discretion to set aside issue estoppel; the court disagrees.

propositions.text: Federal Court acknowledged circumstances to set aside issue estoppel: appeal, material change, or new evidence.
propositions.quote: The Federal Court correctly acknowledged that “there are circumstances where the doctrine of issue estoppel can be set aside, namely in the event of an appeal, a material change in circumstances, or new evidence”

propositions.text: Federal Court considered appellant's arguments and evidence on discretion, including FCA decisions and legislative changes.
propositions.quote: The Federal Court also thoroughly considered Ms. Berenguer’s arguments and evidence justifying the exercise of its discretion, including the impact of the FCA Appeal and Reconsideration Decisions and subsequent legislative and evidentiary changes in the CTA’s dispute resolution process.

propositions.text: No palpable and overriding error by Federal Court in discretion exercise; appellant's insistence on potential injustice does not overcome finality importance.
propositions.quote: We see no basis on which the Federal Court could be said to have committed a palpable and overriding error... Ms. Berenguer’s insistence that the Federal Court erred in failing to consider “potential injustice”... does not overcome... the fundamental importance of finality in the judicial system.

propositions.text: Accepting appellant's arguments would reduce doctrine of finality to naught.
propositions.quote: If accepted, Ms. Berenguer’s arguments and motion would effectively reduce the doctrine of finality to naught.

paragraphs.summary: The Federal Court considered discretion to set aside issue estoppel and found no error, emphasizing finality over appellant's injustice argument.

propositions.text: The court will dismiss the motion to admit fresh evidence and the appeal without costs due to related proceedings.
propositions.quote: Accordingly, we will dismiss the motion to admit fresh evidence and the appeal without costs, given that these proceedings are related to the earlier certification proceedings.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the motion for fresh evidence and the appeal without costs as related to earlier proceedings.
